newsitem.title: USA: Hillary Clinton traveling to Africa Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton traveling to Africa Saturday.

text.p: Hillary Rodham Clinton embarks on Saturday on a six-nation tour of Africa that will underscore U.S. commitment to an active engagement with the continent, the White House announced on Tuesday.
During her March 15-30 trip, President Bill Clinton's wife will visit Senegal, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Uganda and Eritrea. It will mark her ninth solo trip outside the United States.

A White House statement said Mrs. Clinton hopes her visit will stress the importance of democracy and human rights, women's issues and social investments in areas such as education, health care and encouraging small businesses, as well as "our collective commitment to the survival and well-being of children."

"Mrs. Clinton's goodwill trip will underscore the United States' commitment to continued active engagement with the continent and highlight the progress of democracy in the countries she will visit," the White House said.
Among the first lady's planned stops and activities are:
-- Goree Island in Senegal, a hub of much of the African slave trade;
-- Saam Njaay Village in Senegal, where grassroots efforts are under way to train citizens about the institutions of democracy;
-- A tour of projects in Soweto, South Africa, aimed at bringing new opportunities for the people of the township;
-- A tree-planting with South African Archbishop Desmond Tutu, symbolising the nation's path to reconciliation;
-- A speech at the University of Cape Town on South Africa's efforts to build a multi-racial democracy and the importance of South Africa to the United States;
-- A visit with South African President Nelson Mandela to Robben Island, the former prison where Mandela and other South African activists were jailed during apartheid;
-- Projects in Zimbabwe devoted to encouraging "microenterprise" development and family planning;
-- A discussion with members of the U.N. War Crimes Tribunal in Arusha, Tanzania, on the impact of genocide and rape as a war crime;
-- Programmes focusing on AIDS prevention and education in Uganda;
-- A speech in Uganda on the economic, political and social progress in the region and U.S. efforts to support democracy, civil society and social investment in Africa;
-- A visit to Africa's newest country, Eritrea.

The White House said that as on all of her foreign travels, Mrs. Clinton will participate in roundtable discussions with prominent women from the region and non-governmental organisations helping to build civil society. She will pay courtesy calls to prominent government officials.
